title: Underived canonical open base-change compatibility
statement: Let $U'\xrightarrow{g_U}U$ and $X'\xrightarrow{g}X$ form an open-immersion square with open immersions $j:U\to X$ and $j':U'\to X'$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Let $b_{g,F}:g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_U^{-1}F$ be the canonical map of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], and let $\beta_F:j'_!g_U^{-1}F\to g^{-1}j_!F$ be the module base-change map of [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] for this square, read through the identifications $\kappa$ of the etale extensions by zero along $j$ and $j'$ with $j_!$ and $j'_!$ [lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement]. Then $b_{g,F}=\beta_F^{-1}$. More explicitly, under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ the map $b_{g,F}^{-1}$ is the transpose of $s_g\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})$, where $\eta_{j,F}:F\to j^{-1}j_!F$ is the extension-by-zero unit and $s_g:g_U^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ is the module-linear cartesian inverse-image identification. After identifying both restrictions with $g_U^{-1}F$ through these units and $s_g$, the restriction of $b_{g,F}$ is the identity.

proof.text: The open and etale lower shriek functors and their adjunctions are the same localization Kan-extension model for an open immersion. The specified comparison kappa is whiskering an identity by sheafification, hence it is the identity natural transformation (Functor.whiskerRight_id). In the definition of chosenSquareEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap, replace the two kappas by identities and simplify their inverses and whiskerings componentwise. The result is the open base-change map, whose inverse-conjugate definition is definitionally chosenSquareEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMate. This proves chosenSquareEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap_eq_mate without changing the specified comparison.

On the standard fiber-product square, chosenSquareEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMate_pullback is reflexivity: flipping the flipped commutative square gives the square used in etaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap, and the composite adjunctions are identical.

For a cartesian square, install the isomorphism assertions for both kappas from their adjunction-agreement theorem and the isomorphism assertion for the open base-change map. The three factors in the transported map are invertible, so their composite is invertible. This proves isIso_chosenSquareEtaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap.

Construct the IsPullback witness from the chosen cartesian square. Use the already proved unit_map_openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeMap_app in the module-valued coefficient category. It says exactly that the open base-change map has transpose the pulled-back unit followed by squareUpperStarIso, and proves the second conjunct of derivedExtensionZeroBaseChangeUnderivedCompatibility.

By Step 1 the transported etale map equals the open map. NatIso.isIso_inv_app identifies the inverse natural transformation component with the inverse component, and IsIso.inv_eq_inv transfers that equality to the inverse maps. This proves the first conjunct. For the third conjunct, replace the pulled-back unit followed by the square isomorphism using Step 4. Reassociate and combine the two upperStar maps by functoriality. The base-change component followed by its inverse is the identity, so its image is the identity. The remaining extension unit followed by its inverse is the identity by the open-immersion unit isomorphism. This is precisely the required restriction identity.

I also read unit sk-prop-sf-cbc, the parent cor and its main-20261015 blueprint text, and Stacks 03S3, 03S5, 0F70, 03S6 (etale-cohomology) and 03DI (sites-modules). I recomputed Steps 1, 3 and 5. Step 1: the exchange transpose formula, with s_g=θ in the right direction. Step 3: naturality plus the triangle identity gives δ=s_A∘g_U^{-1}η_{j,F}. Step 5: a^{-1}∘j'^{-1}(b)∘d=id. Edge cases checked: U empty, F=0, Λ=0, g=id, j=id. Fault 1 (C3/E6, silent identification): b uses the explicit open-immersion j_! and adjunction (lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction). β (def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map) uses the étale sum extension and the adjunction of lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives, whose statement does not give a unit. In slopmaster2 these are separate constructions (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction vs etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction) and no lemma relates them. Step 2 and Steps 4–5 equated the two units and counits without a citation. The identification is true by Stacks 03DI. Repair: I added the statement-only node lem-cbc-open-extension-zero-etale-adjunction-agreement. It says the sectionwise identification κ: j_!→j^et_! is a natural isomorphism that takes units to units and counits to counits. The item statement now reads β through κ (conclusion unchanged, nothing weakened), and Step 2 cites the new node. Fault 2 (Step 4): the delivery used the module hom bijection for b, which is a priori only an abelian map, and cited the fibre-product-only lemma lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules for β invertible. Step 4 now compares underlying abelian maps through the Λ-independent sectionwise bijection, and gets β invertible from b being an isomorphism. I recomputed proof_deps. The new node records only grep searches, because LeanSearch, Loogle and LeanFinder are not reachable here; it may need the other two search kinds added on the Codex machine. Mathlib's leftAdjointUniq is a generic iso of left adjoints; it does not give that iso as κ, so the verdict is no match. I accepted the three declared tool uses.
